snippet.title: India's Trump Card Against the US | Sunset Clause Explained
snippet.description:
The India-US trade deal has entered a crucial phase, but this time New Delhi is not willing to accept a "take it or leave it" approach. At the centre of the negotiations is the Sunset Clause—a provision that could fundamentally change how India and the United States approach future trade agreements. But what exactly is a Sunset Clause, and why is India insisting on including it?
In this video, we explain how the Sunset Clause works, why India wants periodic reviews instead of a permanent agreement, and how changing US administrations and trade policies have influenced India's negotiating strategy. We also examine why this clause is being seen as a strategic tool to protect India's long-term economic interests while ensuring that future trade relations remain balanced and flexible. Watch till the end to understand why this single legal provision has become one of the most talked-about aspects of the India-US trade negotiations.

snippet.title: Space Is Filling With Junk… And It Could Make Earth’s Orbit Unusable
snippet.description:
Space is no longer empty—it’s becoming dangerously crowded. With record-breaking launches in 2025 by agencies like ISRO and private companies, Low Earth Orbit is now packed with active satellites, dead spacecraft, and debris fragments.

These objects travel at speeds of up to 28,000 km/h—fast enough for even a tiny screw to cause catastrophic damage. Indian satellites alone received over 150,000 collision alerts in a year, while global alerts crossed 160,000.

To avoid disasters, space agencies must constantly perform collision avoidance maneuvers. But if this continues unchecked, we could trigger the Kessler Syndrome—a cascading chain reaction of collisions that could make Earth’s orbit unusable for generations.

Space is no longer just about exploration… it’s about survival.

snippet.title: Iran Has $12 Trillion Buried Underground #oil #geopolitics
snippet.description:
Iran holds 208 billion barrels of proven oil reserves, making it the 3rd largest in the world, right behind Venezuela and Saudi Arabia. But when you add its natural gas, Iran jumps to 2nd on Earth for gas reserves, only behind Russia. 

The combined value of everything sitting underground exceeds $12 trillion. At current consumption rates, the oil alone would last 290 years. Despite this, international sanctions have cost Iran $1.2 trillion in blocked revenue over just 12 years. 

Iran controls 10% of all proven oil on the planet and 15% of all natural gas. All of it largely inaccessible. The U.S. Energy Information Administration published the full breakdown in October 2024. 

Search "EIA Iran Country Analysis 2024" and read it yourself.

snippet.title: What to do if you live in the path of a volcano - Arianna Soldati
snippet.description:
Explore 3 strategies to control the flow of lava, and how scientists are using them to protect communities from future eruptions.

--

In December 2023, Icelandic citizens experienced their worst nightmare: a volcanic fissure opened and began spewing lava fountains 100 meters tall. While the molten rock narrowly avoided a small town, Iceland wasn’t willing to leave anyone's fate to chance again and began preparing for future eruptions. Arianna Soldati explores 3 potential strategies to control these red-hot rivers of destruction.

snippet.title: Running on empty: How the Middle East war is squeezing jet fuel markets, with Susan Bell
snippet.description:
Join us for our annual Summits in Singapore, Houston and London: https://rystad.info/48VVL1M

Let’s Talk Energy and take the pulse of the aviation industry as it struggles to source enough fuel as the Middle East war dries up global supplies.   

Airlines are facing their biggest test since Covid. While Brent futures are up 70+% this year, jet fuel prices have doubled in Europe and risen 110% in Asia over 2025 averages.  

The situation caused the CEO of United Airlines to warn ticket prices could increase by about 20%. Lufthansa canceled 20,000 flights that it said were no longer profitable.  US budget carrier Spirit Airlines stopped flying altogether after declaring bankruptcy. And finally, Fatih Birol, head of the International Energy Agency (IEA), warned that Europe could start running out of jet fuel in as little as six weeks.  

+ How has the war hit jet fuel supplies, and why has the price squeeze been even worse for jet than for crude?
+ How are refiners reacting to the shortage, and do high prices necessarily mean high margins for the sector?
+ What can countries do – short of grounding flights – to manage this market and help consumers cope with the runup in prices?

snippet.description:
India’s aviation sector is under massive pressure as Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) prices continue to rise sharply. Major airlines like IndiGo and Air India have reportedly raised concerns with the government over skyrocketing fuel costs.

ATF, which earlier accounted for nearly 40% of airline operational expenses, has now surged to almost 55–60% after the growing West Asia tensions and the Strait of Hormuz crisis disrupted crude oil supply chains.

The problem is not just expensive fuel. India’s ATF pricing is linked to international benchmark MOPAG, making airlines vulnerable to global oil shocks. While domestic fuel pricing remains partially controlled, international routes are facing the full impact — pushing airlines into heavy losses.

Now airlines are demanding the return of the crack margin band, along with temporary cuts in excise duty and state VAT.

Will the government step in before India’s aviation sector enters a deeper crisis?

snippet.title: How did ancient civilizations brew beer? - Malcolm Purinton

Trace the history and evolution of beer, from its first known existence 13,000 years ago to the modern beverage we know today.

snippet.title: Information Systems vs Information Technology | What Is the Difference?
snippet.description:
Information Systems and Information Technology are closely connected.
But they are not identical.
Information Technology focuses mainly on technological tools such as computers, software, networks, databases, and cloud platforms.
Information Systems focus on how technology, people, data, and business processes work together.

Here’s the reality:
Information Technology is a component of Information Systems, while Information Systems focus on using technology to solve organisational problems and achieve business objectives.
In this lecture, we compare Information Systems and Information Technology and explain their roles, differences, examples, and career paths.

What You’ll Learn
• what Information Systems means
• what Information Technology means
• the main difference between IS and IT
• how both fields work together
• examples of IS and IT in real organisations
• career differences between the two fields

What Is Information Technology?
Information Technology focuses on the technological infrastructure used to create, process, store, secure, and exchange data.
It includes:
• computers
• servers
• software
• networks
• databases
• cloud platforms
• cybersecurity tools
• technical support
IT professionals usually focus on keeping technology reliable, secure, and functional.

What Is Information Systems?
Information Systems focus on how organisations use:
• people
• technology
• data
• processes
• policies
• business knowledge
The goal is not simply to operate technology.
The goal is to use information to improve decisions, productivity, communication, and performance.

The Main Difference
Information Technology asks:
“How does the technology work?”
Information Systems asks:
“How can people and organisations use this technology effectively?”

Simple Example
Imagine a restaurant using a digital ordering platform.
The Information Technology side includes:
• tablets
• internet connections
• kitchen printers
• ordering software
• databases
• payment systems

The Information System includes:
• customers placing orders
• staff receiving requests
• kitchen workflows
• menu and price data
• payment processes
• management reports
• the technology connecting everything
The technology is important.
But the full system includes much more than technology.

Key Differences
Main Focus

Information Technology:
Technology and technical infrastructure

Information Systems:
Business needs, people, data, processes, and technology

Main Objective
Information Technology:
Keep systems operational, secure, and efficient

Information Systems:
Use information to solve problems and support organisational goals

Typical Questions
Information Technology:
How should we configure the network?

Information Systems:
How can this system improve the business process?
Skills

Information Technology:
Programming, networking, cybersecurity, cloud computing, and system maintenance

Information Systems:
Business analysis, process design, data analysis, project management, and technology strategy

Career Examples
Information Technology Careers
• network engineer
• cybersecurity analyst
• cloud engineer
• systems administrator
• IT support specialist
• software developer

Information Systems Careers
• business analyst
• systems analyst
• IT project manager
• information systems manager
• ERP consultant
• technology consultant

Some careers overlap because both fields depend on technology and business knowledge.

The Real Shift
• from treating IS and IT as identical → understanding their different roles
• from technology alone → technology connected with people and processes
• from maintaining systems → improving organisational performance
• from technical tools → business solutions

Reality Check
• Information Systems cannot work without technology
• Information Technology has little value if it does not support real needs
• strong technical systems can still fail because of poor processes
• employees can reject systems that are difficult to use
• organisations need both technical and business expertise

Why This Matters
Understanding the difference helps students and professionals:
• choose the right degree or career
• understand organisational technology roles
• communicate more clearly with technical teams
• design better business systems
• avoid treating every business problem as only a technical problem

Because at the end:
Information Technology provides the tools, but Information Systems determine how those tools create value for people and organisations.

snippet.title: India’s BIGGEST Political Shift? 815 Lok Sabha Seats & Delimitation Explained
snippet.description:
Is India heading toward a major transformation in its democratic structure?

The government is planning to introduce new Bills that could increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from 543 to 815 seats. Along with this comes delimitation — the process of redrawing constituencies based on population.

But here’s the big question:
What happens when the fixed rule of delimitation after every Census is removed?

This could mean future governments decide:
 • When delimitation happens
 • Which Census data is used

Southern states are already raising concerns — having controlled population growth, they fear losing representation, while northern states may gain more seats.

The government says balance will be maintained — but how exactly? That’s still unclear.

This isn’t just about numbers.
It’s about representation, fairness, and the future of India’s democracy.

👉 What do YOU think about this possible change? Share your thoughts in the comments!
